title: The shroud image was made by a burst of neutrons at the resurrection
summary: Whitley Strieber tells of The shroud image was made by a burst of neutrons at the resurrection, about c. 33 AD at Jerusalem, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: The shroud is the single strangest thing on planet Earth. And it is that way because it records the moment a human being whose body had expired transformed into a being of light.

related.note: Both are about what the Shroud records of the man in it, but Strieber says it shows a body that had died and turned into light, while this telling says the man was alive.

plain: Whitley Strieber, an author known for writing about strange encounters, calls the Shroud of Turin, an old linen cloth bearing the faint image of a man and believed by many to be Jesus's burial cloth, the single strangest thing on Earth. He says it records the moment a dead human body transformed into a being of light, with the image made by a burst of neutrons at the resurrection in Jerusalem. If true, it would mean the cloth is a physical record of a person's body changing into something else.
